title: Release the ODOC-231 git-grounded version control work: version bump, changelog, publish
description:
Routed by opum-agent 2026-09-20: the LCLI-546 epic is all implementation and carries no record for the release that delivers it. Filed so the release states the path it will take rather than discovering it at tag time.

THE PATH THIS RELEASE TAKES, and it is the manual one. LCLI-482 (OIDC trusted publishing is broken by GitHub immutable subject claims) is still To Do -- confirmed by reading the record, not assumed. So this goes out through the manual publish path with NO provenance attestation, exactly as 0.8.0, 0.7.0, 0.6.2 and 0.6.1 did. This task does not solve LCLI-482 and must not be blocked on it; it is required to SAY that it shipped without provenance, so the gap stays visible instead of being rediscovered.

Current published state, read rather than remembered: npm dist-tags.latest = 0.8.0, package.json = 0.8.0, and the tag list holds v0.8.0 v0.7.0 v0.6.2 v0.6.1 v0.6.0. ODOC-231 changes lore's store of record and accepts a backward incompatibility (see LCLI-561), so the version this cuts is a MINOR at minimum; the decision between 0.9.0 and 1.0.0 belongs with the release and should be stated in it, not defaulted.

TWO COUPLINGS THE RELEASE MUST HONOUR, both of which fire at tag time and neither of which is implementation work:

1. THE MARKETPLACE HANDSHAKE (LCLI-469). opum-marketplace federates this repository's skills/ directory BY TAG -- its marketplace.json pins a tag name and scripts/check-federated-content.mjs re-resolves tag ref -> tag object -> commit -> root tree -> skills/ subtree against a recorded baseline. Their check does NOT go red when we tag, because the pinned ref is immutable; the handshake exists so their eventual pin bump is bookkeeping rather than archaeology. At tag-cut time send the tag name, the tag object SHA, the commit it peels to, and the resolved skills/ tree SHA -- numbers to be re-resolved, not trusted -- then a SECOND message when npm actually publishes, because they deliberately hold the pin until dist-tags.latest moves.

2. THE LOCKFILE PROBLEM (LCLI-544): a version bump cannot prove its lockfile is current, because the bumped versions are not published yet. Read that record before bumping rather than rediscovering it.

Sequencing is reserved to lore-cli by the ADR. This depends on all five epic children plus LCLI-560 (the spec retirement), so it cannot be started early; it does NOT depend on LCLI-561, which is owed for the already-shipped 0.8.0 and should go out ahead of this release, not with it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The version to cut is decided and stated with its reasoning (minor vs major), given that ODOC-231 accepts a backward incompatibility rather than defaulting to a bump size
CHANGELOG records the ODOC-231 work and explicitly names the accepted incompatibility, cross-referencing LCLI-561
The release record states that it shipped via the manual publish path with NO provenance attestation, and cites LCLI-482 as the open reason
LCLI-544 is read and its lockfile constraint is satisfied or explicitly waived before the bump
The LCLI-469 marketplace handshake is sent at tag-cut with tag name, tag object SHA, peeled commit and resolved skills/ tree SHA, and a SECOND message once npm dist-tags.latest actually moves
npm dist-tags.latest is re-resolved after publish and matches the cut version -- read from the registry, not from the publish command output

opum-cli-e2e is told BEFORE publish, so their qualification-matrix baseline re-promotion (their TASK-77, baselines/ci-linux-x64/) rides alongside rather than reddening their required context after the fact

implementationNotes: opum-cli-e2e (2026-09-20) reports a hard coupling at publish time: under their TASK-77, baselines/ci-linux-x64/ gates every run and the required context 'qualification matrix vs the committed baseline' compares against it. When LCLI-548's committed citations and the provenance work reach a published lore their matrix installs, these rows change verdict and their gate reddens CORRECTLY -- a baseline re-promotion must ride in its own PR. Rows they pin today, all against the retention cache this epic retires: suites/30-lore-lifecycle.mjs:365-378 (retain then list round-trip); suites/31-lore-retrieval.mjs:177 (snapshotKey matches ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$), :200 (list enumerates distinct keys), :218 (changed reports the delta), :235 and :251 (provenance traces a retained concept; fails closed against an UNRETAINED snapshot), :266 (delete removes exactly the named projection); suites/11-contract-lore.mjs:74-89 (provenance --kind and --snapshot both required:true at their live manifest paths) plus a snapshot list row at :151. Nothing on their side asserts the cap of 16, so removing it is free. Since LCLI-482 is open the publish is manual, so there is no automated path that could surprise them -- the notification is the only control and it is now AC[7] rather than a remembered courtesy.
